hero.eyebrow: For busy professionals with desk-related pain
hero.heading: Chiropractic that works around your working day
hero.lead: Neck, back and shoulder pain from long hours at a desk? Book online in under a minute, park right outside, and see the same chiropractor every visit. Evenings until 7pm, Saturday mornings, and a clear treatment plan — not an endless course of care.
hero.note: New here? First appointments are 60 min consultations designed for new patients.

pills: Anyone with neck, back or shoulder pain

why.heading: I've designed the chiropractic experience around people who work.
why.quote: I'll make getting treatment as easy as possible — and I'll only recommend the care you actually need.

whatITreat.heading: Evidence-informed care for the pain that comes with desk work.
whatITreat.note: Not sure it's right for you? I'll tell you honestly — including if a physio or your GP is the better fit.

cards.label: Follow-up treatment
cards.description: Ongoing treatment appointments as part of your care plan.

questions.a: A practitioner trained to assess and treat problems with your muscles, joints and spine — usually with hands-on manipulation, mobilisation and exercise advice.
Both can help with pain. Chiropractic focuses more on hands-on spinal and joint treatment. If I think physio — or a GP — is the better route, I'll say so and point you there.
No — chiropractors are separately regulated, registered practitioners. I diagnose and treat musculoskeletal problems, and refer you on when something is outside that.
